overview: LiquidSense Dev's NoFall is a 13-mode fall-damage bypass built on the C03 onGround flag. The default SpoofGround mode rewrites every outgoing C03PacketPlayer so onGround is true, which resets the server-side fall distance before damage applies; the NoGround mode's branch is byte-identical to SpoofGround, a copy-paste artifact that also forces the flag true despite its name. The packet modes (Packet, Hypixel, CubeCraft, AAC, AAC3.3.11, AAC3.3.15, Spartan, NewPacket) send their own C03 or C04 claims past fall-distance thresholds, AAC4.4.0 buffers the whole C03 stream while falling and flushes it with onGround rewritten true on landing, LAAC pulls the player to the ground with motionY -6, and MLG predicts the landing with a FallingPlayer simulation and places a water bucket or web automatically. A liquid-collision guard disables every mode while the player's bounding box touches liquid.

sections.p: The onPacket handler rewrites packet fields in place before the send. In SpoofGround mode every C03PacketPlayer that passes through has onGround set to true, whether it carried a position, a look or neither; the vanilla server processes an onGround-true move by resetting the player's fallDistance, which is the entire damage-dodge mechanism. The NoGround case is a verbatim copy of the SpoofGround case: both set the flag true, so the mode named for never claiming ground claims it on every packet. The rewrite applies to the client's normal tick traffic, so no extra packets are emitted in these two modes, and the flag rides the existing C03 stream.

The send modes construct their own packets once the client fallDistance passes a threshold. Packet, Hypixel, CubeCraft and AAC emit C03PacketPlayer(true) past fallDistance 2 (Hypixel first checks realDist from a motion-derived accumulator and skips the void, CubeCraft also flips the local onGround field false, and AAC follows the claim with a three-tick motionY 0.1 state machine). AAC3.3.11 zeroes motionX and motionZ and sends C04 with y minus 10E-4 plus a bare C03(true); AAC3.3.15 sends a C04 whose y is Double.NaN with onGround false and sets fallDistance to -9999; Spartan, rate-limited to once per 10 ticks, sends C04 with y plus 10 and then y minus 10, both onGround true. AAC4.4.0 is the fakelag mode: while falling over non-void terrain it cancels every C03 and parks it in a list, and on landing flushes the list, rewriting each packet's onGround to true first.

The MLG mode is a full water-clutch automaton. Once fallDistance exceeds the MinMLGHeight setting (default 5), it builds a FallingPlayer from the current position and motion, simulates the fall with vanilla physics (gravity 0.08, drag 0.91, motionY 0.98 factor) and ray-traces the trajectory across the body corners to find the first upward-facing block within reach. It then hotbar-switches to a water bucket or web (C09 held-item change), faces the target with RotationUtils and places the item (C08) at the predicted landing block. The mode runs at most every 10 ticks. The liquid guard at the top of onUpdate and onMove returns early when the player's bounding box or the row below it touches a BlockLiquid, and the LAAC mode instead zeroes horizontal motion and slams motionY to -6 while falling so the player lands before damage accrues.

files.label: NoFall.java
files.explanation: The module is the full dispatch: a ListValue with thirteen registered modes, an onPacket rewrite path, an onUpdate switch, an onMotionUpdate handler that runs the NewPacket accumulator and the AAC4.4.0 fakelag state machine plus the MLG clutch, an onMove handler for the LAAC mode, and the helper predicates (isBlockUnder, inVoid, isVoid, inAir, getJumpEffect). The state fields are lastFall, the spartanTimer and mlgTimer TickTimers, the fakelag boolean, the packets buffer and the currentMlgRotation, currentMlgItemIndex and currentMlgBlock targets. The modeValue default is SpoofGround, and the getTag method returns the selected mode name for the module list.

files.label: FallingPlayer.java (MLG fall predictor)
files.explanation: The MLG mode's trajectory simulator. The constructor captures the current position, motion, yaw, strafe and forward input, and calculateForTick (lines 39-72) steps the state with the exact vanilla airborne physics: strafe and forward decay by 0.98, gravity subtracts 0.08, motion decays by 0.91 with the motionY 0.98 factor. findCollision (lines 74-109) advances the simulation up to the requested tick count and ray-traces each tick's segment from the center and the four body corners plus four half-corner points, returning the first block whose top face is hit, together with the tick index. The NoFall MLG mode uses the collision result to decide reachability and to pick the placement target; the class is shared infrastructure that the module consumes but does not modify.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (block-cache ground truth)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly never trusts the C03 onGround bit. The from and to ground states come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround() (lines 138-140), a block-cache scan at minY minus the yOnGround epsilon, and the vertical allowance comes from vDistRel, which seeds the allowed distance from the previous move's momentum and only accepts a handful of named envelopes (zero-y move on ground, jump, step-up, riptide launch); the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back. The SpoofGround and NoGround rewrites claim ground over open air, which the block cache contradicts, so the descent is still scored against the fall envelope and the claim buys no leniency. The packet modes' C03(true) sends are the same shape, and AAC3.3.11's C04 with y minus 10E-4 shifts by a sub-0.03 amount the server ignores for movement while the onGround true still applies, so the claim is what the envelope rejects. The companion check moving/player/NoFall.java keeps its own noFallMaxY and noFallFallDistance bookkeeping and deals the fall damage itself, so zeroing the client fallDistance field never cancels NCP's accounting.

countering.label: NoFall (ground-location cross-check)
countering.explanation: Vrekt's NoFall compares three independently derived states: MovingListener computes ground from the world (LocationHelper.isOnGround) and stores the location as groundLocation whenever grounded, PacketListener records the raw packet flag into MovingData via setFlyingClientOnGround, and Bukkit tracks the server-side fall distance. NoFall.check() fires when the vertical distance from the last grounded location is at least 3.0 blocks, the player is descending, Vrekt's own ground state says airborne, the client claimed onGround and the server fall distance is exactly 0.0, producing the violation 'Fall distance is 0 while not onGround. (Client faked)' and player.damage(toGround) on cancel. Every flag-rewrite mode zeroes the server fall distance through vanilla onGround handling, so the first descent past 3.0 blocks below the grounded location, with Vrekt's own ground airborne and the server distance at zero, trips the violation. The 3.0-block descent requirement is the tolerance: short hops and real landings pass, and the bypass is claiming ground only when the position truly touches a block.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (predicted-position trace)
countering.explanation: Hawk's GroundSpoof derives its own ground state on every MoveEvent. For position updates it reads event.isOnGroundReally(), already lag-compensated; for flag-only updates it runs AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally on the predicted position with the predicted velocity Y at a 0.001 tolerance. When the event claims onGround but the trace reports air, the check re-tests the pre-move position with the Y already clipped (mirroring the client's clip-then-flag order), skips step and web-phasing cases, and punishes with a rubber-band. With the preventNoFall setting enabled, setNotOnGround rewrites the raw packet bytes so the onGround flag is forced false on the wire, actively undoing the SpoofGround and NoGround rewrites before the server processes them. Claims within the 0.02 tolerance of real terrain pass, which is the legitimate-landing band.

countering.label: NoFall (post-prediction collision check)
countering.explanation: Grim's NoFall runs as a PacketReceiveListener on PLAYER_FLYING and PLAYER_ROTATION after the prediction engine has simulated the tick. For any packet that claims onGround true and carries no position change (wrapper.isOnGround() && !wrapper.hasPositionChanged()), it builds a 0.6 by 0.001 feet box at the simulated position, expands it by the movement threshold and collides it against the compensated world plus nearby hard entities; on no collision it flags with the 10-tick setback and, when modification is allowed, rewrites the onGround bit to false and re-encodes. The Packet, Hypixel, CubeCraft and AAC modes' bare C03(true) packets are flag-only PLAYER_FLYING packets, the exact case this check handles, and the AAC3.3.11 pair's bare C03(true) trails the position C04, so the claim half is caught. The position-bearing claims (the C04s themselves, AAC3.3.15's NaN y and the AAC4.4.0 flush) are deliberately skipped by this check and land in the prediction-based GroundSpoof domain instead.
